hints: Sort weights, then look at the lightest and heaviest unassigned child.
If they fit together, placing them together is safe; otherwise the heaviest must ride alone.
Remove the heaviest each time and count one gondola.
analogy: Pair the heaviest rider with the lightest possible partner; if even that partner is too heavy, nobody else can help.
example: For weights 2,3,7,9 with limit 10: pair 2+7, while 3 and 9 need separate gondolas: 3 total.
algorithm: Sort weights and move pointers inward. Count one gondola for the heaviest; also consume the lightest if their sum is at most x.
correctness: The heaviest child must use a gondola now. Pairing them with the lightest feasible child preserves the most capacity for the remaining children; if that pair fails, the heaviest rides alone.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(1) pointer space beyond sorting.
